sections.title: Goal and intuition
sections.learning_objective: State inputs, outputs, assumptions and small example traces.
sections.markdown: Before choosing an algorithm, agree on what counts as a correct answer. A contract states inputs, outputs, bounds and awkward cases. A trace then follows one small input through the proposed steps. This prevents solving the wrong task quickly. No prior sorting or graph knowledge is needed: our first examples use integer arithmetic and a fully provided function wrapper.
key_points: A method that works only when a >= b does not implement absolute distance.

sections.title: A worked example and why it works
sections.learning_objective: State inputs, outputs, assumptions and small example traces.
sections.markdown: Define the distance between integer positions a and b as a nonnegative integer. For positions 3 and 8, subtracting gives -5; taking its absolute value gives 5. Reversing the positions still gives 5. Equal positions give 0. In Python, abs(x) returns the magnitude of x, so `return abs(a - b)` matches the contract. Simply returning a - b fails when a is smaller. The work and extra storage are constant for the bounded integers used here; passing these cases is not a proof about arbitrary huge-integer cost.

sections.title: Guided practice, independent practice and revision
sections.learning_objective: State inputs, outputs, assumptions and small example traces.
sections.markdown:
Guided: trace a=9, b=4: difference 5, magnitude 5, return integer 5. Independent: state the contract for remaining capacity when used may exceed capacity.

<details><summary>Contract and checked examples</summary>Inputs are two nonnegative integers. Return max(0, capacity - used), never a negative capacity. For capacity 8 and used 3 return 5; for used 11 return 0. Python max(0, difference) chooses the larger value. The exact signature and bounds must be written before submission.</details>

Revision: read the return type, list valid input ranges, trace normal/equal/boundary cases, and construct a counterexample to a tempting wrong method. Hidden tests supplement a clear contract; they cannot rescue an ambiguous statement. Do not print or return a string when an integer is requested.
